# New Orleans Pelicans Season Preview - A Team With No Direction

Locked On Fantasy Basketball, 2026-08-03, 35:35. https://youtu.be/5QU-jta-lWM

## Summary

Josh Lloyd and Jake Madison preview the New Orleans Pelicans, who had a very quiet offseason. Jake argues the team is stuck between two timelines: a win-now core of Zion Williamson, Trey Murphy and Herb Jones, and a rebuild core of Jeremiah Fears and Derik Queen. They say Zion and Queen do not fit together, the roster lacks shooting and defensive rebounding, and Dejounte Murray blocks Fears from a lead guard role. Yves Missi is named as the player most likely to gain a bigger role, possibly as the starting center under new coach Jamahl Mosley's defense-first scheme. Jake sees this as a make or break year for Zion and predicts about 34 wins. A Trey Murphy trade is possible only if a team makes a huge offer.

## Rules and methods

- [6:55](https://youtu.be/5QU-jta-lWM?t=415) Rookies and second-year players usually do not help a team win. The leap tends to come in year three, so teams trying to win often bench their young players.
  > "rookies don't help you win games. Secondyear players don't really help you win games. It's that third year"
- [32:47](https://youtu.be/5QU-jta-lWM?t=1967) A player on a cheap contract is worth the most in trades early in the deal. His trade value drops as his next contract gets closer.
  > "the closer you get to having to pay him his next deal, the value goes down."
- [25:23](https://youtu.be/5QU-jta-lWM?t=1523) Defensive scheme can affect a big man's rebounding. A switch-everything scheme pulls centers out to the perimeter and lowers their defensive rebounding rate.
  > "So, I do think scheme can maybe help him a little bit"
- [30:23](https://youtu.be/5QU-jta-lWM?t=1823) Teams that keep competing late in the season can pile up wins in March and April against teams that are tanking.
  > "they were able to rack up those wins in that period of the year when everyone else was trying to lose"
